To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of microelements can influence the interfacial reactions between the solder and substrate and the microelements play an important role on the difference in the interfacial IMC morphology and growth rate.
the microelements addition to the Sn-Ag-based solders influences the interfacially formed intermetallic compounds.

the interfacials intermetallics of the Cu/Sn-0.7Ni and the Cu/Sn0.5Cu0.07Ni0.01Ge solder joints have the same structure of (Cux,Nix)6Sn5, and the Ni addition in the solder can significantly increase the thickness of interfacial IMC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of Ni addition on the intermetallics at the solder/Cu interface.
the influence of microelement addition on the intermetallics formation at the interface between Sn-Ag-based solders and Cu substrate.
the interfacial IMCs and the growth kinetics of IMCs in the Sn-Ag-based solders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of microelements Ni and Ge to the Sn-Ag-Cux solders can improve the interfacial reactions between the solder and Cu substrate.
the microelement Ni plays a key role in the interfacial reactions of Sn-Ag solders.
the microelements addition can influence the interfacial IMCs morphology, but not their growth kinetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microelement Ni can influence the interfacial IMC growth and morphology of the Sn-0.5Ag-3.5Sn-0.07Cu-0.01Ni-0.07Ge/Cu and Sn-3Ag-3.8Sn-0.7Ni/Cu systems.
the addition of microelements Ni and Ge into Sn-3.0Ag solder is effective in inhibiting interfacial reaction, and the effect is better for the solder with Ni than for the solder with Ge.
the addition of Ni and Ge in Sn-Ag-based solders can improve the wetting property and enhance the thermal stability of the interfacials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of microelements (e.g., Ni and Ge) can significantly influence the interfacial microstructure and the interfacial growth kinetics of Sn-Ag based solders.
the interfacially grown Cu6Sn5 is a diffusion-controlled process.
the growth of IMCs in the Sn-3Ag-0.05Cu-0.1Ni-0.1Ge/Cu system follows a parabolic growth law.
